title: 〜ている — be doing (ongoing action); be in a state (result of a change); do regularly
explanation: 〜ている expresses be doing (ongoing action); be in a state (result of a change); do regularly. With action verbs (食べる, 読む) it shows an action in progress; with change verbs (結婚する, 開く, 知る) it shows the resulting state. Polite: 〜ています.
formation: Verb-te + いる

exercises.explanation: 弟は今、部屋でゲームをしています。 means “My younger brother is playing a game in his room now.”. This illustrates 〜ている: be doing (ongoing action); be in a state (result of a change); do regularly. With action verbs (食べる, 読む) it shows an action in progress; with change verbs (結婚する, 開く, 知る) it shows the resulting state. Polite: 〜ています.

title: 〜ほうがいい — had better; should
explanation: 〜ほうがいい expresses had better; should. For advice, the past form (行ったほうがいい) is the usual choice and sounds stronger. The negative uses the ない form, not the past.
formation: Verb-ta / Verb-nai + ほうがいい

examples.text: 熱があるなら、病院に行ったほうがいいですよ。

examples.text: 夜遅くに一人で歩かないほうがいい。
examples.reading: よるおそくにひとりであるかないほうがいい。
examples.translation: You'd better not walk alone late at night.

examples.text: 大事な書類は、コピーしておいたほうがいいですよ。
examples.reading: だいじなしょるいは、コピーしておいたほうがいいですよ。
examples.translation: It's a good idea to make copies of important documents.

title: Subject pronouns
explanation: Subject pronouns distinguish person and number. Spanish often omits them because the verb ending identifies the subject; use an explicit pronoun for contrast or clarity.
formation: yo, tú, él/ella/usted, nosotros/as, vosotros/as, ellos/ellas/ustedes + conjugated verb

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: ___ soy Ana.
I am Ana.
exercises.explanation: Yo soy Ana. — I am Ana. Subject pronouns distinguish person and number. Spanish often omits them because the verb ending identifies the subject; use an explicit pronoun for contrast or clarity.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: ___ somos estudiantes.
We are students.
exercises.explanation: Nosotros somos estudiantes. — We are students. Subject pronouns distinguish person and number. Spanish often omits them because the verb ending identifies the subject; use an explicit pronoun for contrast or clarity.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: ___ son médicas.
They (female) are doctors.
exercises.explanation: Ellas son médicas. — They (female) are doctors. Subject pronouns distinguish person and number. Spanish often omits them because the verb ending identifies the subject; use an explicit pronoun for contrast or clarity.

exercises.prompt: Which pronoun normally takes third-person singular agreement?
exercises.explanation: Formal singular usted takes third-person singular verb forms.

exercises.prompt: Translate: We (a group of women) speak Spanish.
exercises.explanation: Nosotras is feminine plural; hablamos agrees with a first-person plural subject.

title: Irregular preterite stems

title: Preterite spelling changes
explanation: Verbs ending in -car, -gar, and -zar change spelling before the yo ending -é to preserve pronunciation. Other regular preterite forms keep the original consonant.
formation: -car → -qué; -gar → -gué; -zar → -cé in yo preterite

exercises.explanation: Yo llegué tarde anoche. — I arrived late last night. Verbs ending in -car, -gar, and -zar change spelling before the yo ending -é to preserve pronunciation. Other regular preterite forms keep the original consonant.

exercises.explanation: Yo empecé a leer ayer. — I began reading yesterday. Verbs ending in -car, -gar, and -zar change spelling before the yo ending -é to preserve pronunciation. Other regular preterite forms keep the original consonant.

title: Preterite versus imperfect
explanation: The preterite presents an event as a completed whole; the imperfect supplies a continuing situation or habit. The same activity can use either tense depending on viewpoint, so time words alone are not an infallible rule.
formation: background in imperfect + completed event in preterite

The same activity can use either tense depending on viewpoint, so time words alone are not an infallible rule.

exercises.prompt:

The same activity can use either tense depending on viewpoint, so time words alone are not an infallible rule.

title: Present perfect

formation: he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han + past participle

exercises.prompt:

exercises.explanation: Ella ha comido ya. — She has already eaten. The present perfect combines present haber with a past participle. Its distribution varies by region: in much of Spain it commonly connects a past event to an unfinished present period, while other varieties often prefer the preterite.

title: Negating statements with δεν
explanation: Δεν negates an ordinary indicative statement and normally comes before the verb or a short object pronoun. Use μην in negative να-clauses and prohibitions instead; δεν is not a universal replacement for every English “not”.
formation: δεν + (object pronoun) + indicative verb; δεν + θα + future verb

title: Duration continuing until now: εδώ και
explanation: Εδώ και followed by a duration can describe a situation that began earlier and continues now. Greek commonly uses the present in this construction, where English may use “have been”; do not confuse it with πριν από, which locates an event a duration ago.
formation: present situation + εδώ και + duration

examples.text: Μένω στην Αθήνα εδώ και δύο χρόνια.
examples.translation: I have been living in Athens for two years.

examples.text: Μαθαίνω ελληνικά εδώ και έναν χρόνο.
examples.translation: I have been learning Greek for a year.
We have been waiting for half an hour.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: Μένω στην Αθήνα εδώ ___ δύο χρόνια.
I have been living in Athens for two years.
exercises.explanation: Μένω στην Αθήνα εδώ και δύο χρόνια. — I have been living in Athens for two years. Εδώ και followed by a duration can describe a situation that began earlier and continues now. Greek commonly uses the present in this construction, where English may use “have been”; do not confuse it with πριν από, which locates an event a duration ago.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: Μαθαίνω ελληνικά εδώ και ___ χρόνο.
I have been learning Greek for a year.
exercises.explanation: Μαθαίνω ελληνικά εδώ και έναν χρόνο. — I have been learning Greek for a year. Εδώ και followed by a duration can describe a situation that began earlier and continues now. Greek commonly uses the present in this construction, where English may use “have been”; do not confuse it with πριν από, which locates an event a duration ago.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: Περιμένουμε εδώ και ___ ώρα.
We have been waiting for half an hour.
exercises.explanation: Περιμένουμε εδώ και μισή ώρα. — We have been waiting for half an hour. Εδώ και followed by a duration can describe a situation that began earlier and continues now. Greek commonly uses the present in this construction, where English may use “have been”; do not confuse it with πριν από, which locates an event a duration ago.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase marks a duration continuing to the present?
exercises.explanation: Εδώ και gives elapsed duration for a continuing situation.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means “I arrived two days ago” rather than “I have been here for two days”?
choices: Είμαι εδώ εδώ και δύο μέρες.
exercises.explanation: Πριν από locates a completed arrival two days before now.

title: Always, often and every day
explanation: Πάντα, συχνά and μερικές φορές describe frequency, while κάθε with a singular noun means “every”. Frequency expressions can move for emphasis, but κάθε itself is invariable and does not take a plural ending.
formation: πάντα / συχνά / μερικές φορές + clause; κάθε + singular time noun

examples.translation: We often go to the park.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: Διαβάζω ___ μέρα.
I study every day.
exercises.explanation: Διαβάζω κάθε μέρα. — I study every day. Πάντα, συχνά and μερικές φορές describe frequency, while κάθε with a singular noun means “every”. Frequency expressions can move for emphasis, but κάθε itself is invariable and does not take a plural ending.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: Πηγαίνουμε ___ στο πάρκο.
We often go to the park.
exercises.explanation: Πηγαίνουμε συχνά στο πάρκο. — We often go to the park. Πάντα, συχνά and μερικές φορές describe frequency, while κάθε with a singular noun means “every”. Frequency expressions can move for emphasis, but κάθε itself is invariable and does not take a plural ending.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: ___ φορές τρώω έξω.
Sometimes I eat out.
exercises.explanation: Μερικές φορές τρώω έξω. — Sometimes I eat out. Πάντα, συχνά and μερικές φορές describe frequency, while κάθε with a singular noun means “every”. Frequency expressions can move for emphasis, but κάθε itself is invariable and does not take a plural ending.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correctly formed expression “every week”.
exercises.explanation: Κάθε is invariable and is followed here by singular εβδομάδα.

exercises.prompt: Which adverb means “always”?
exercises.explanation: Πάντα expresses frequency; χθες and αύριο locate time, and εδώ locates place.

title: Clock time: στη μία and στις δύο
explanation: To state the time, use είναι μία for one o’clock and είναι δύο, τρεις and so on for other hours. To say when an event occurs, use στη μία but στις δύο; half past follows the gender of the understood ώρα, giving μία και μισή.
formation: είναι μία / δύο; στη μία / στις δύο; και τέταρτο / και μισή

examples.translation: The lesson starts at one o’clock.
The train leaves at two o’clock.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: Το μάθημα αρχίζει ___ μία.
The lesson starts at one o’clock.
exercises.explanation: Το μάθημα αρχίζει στη μία. — The lesson starts at one o’clock. To state the time, use είναι μία for one o’clock and είναι δύο, τρεις and so on for other hours. To say when an event occurs, use στη μία but στις δύο; half past follows the gender of the understood ώρα, giving μία και μισή.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: Το τρένο φεύγει ___ δύο.
The train leaves at two o’clock.
exercises.explanation: Το τρένο φεύγει στις δύο. — The train leaves at two o’clock. To state the time, use είναι μία for one o’clock and είναι δύο, τρεις and so on for other hours. To say when an event occurs, use στη μία but στις δύο; half past follows the gender of the understood ώρα, giving μία και μισή.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: Είναι μία και ___.
It is half past one.
exercises.explanation: Είναι μία και μισή. — It is half past one. To state the time, use είναι μία for one o’clock and είναι δύο, τρεις and so on for other hours. To say when an event occurs, use στη μία but στις δύο; half past follows the gender of the understood ώρα, giving μία και μισή.

exercises.prompt: Choose “at three o’clock”.
exercises.explanation: Hours beyond one use plural στις; the feminine numeral is τρεις.

exercises.prompt: Complete: Είναι δύο και ___. (“It is quarter past two.”)
exercises.explanation: The expression for quarter past is και τέταρτο.

title: Weekdays and dates
explanation: A definite accusative weekday can place an event on a day, as in τη Δευτέρα, while στις plus a numeral expresses many calendar dates. Month names commonly appear in the genitive after a date; recurring weekdays can also use plural forms such as τις Δευτέρες.
formation: τη Δευτέρα / την Τρίτη; στις δύο Μαΐου; τις Δευτέρες for Mondays

examples.text: Τα γενέθλιά μου είναι στις δύο Μαΐου.
examples.translation: My birthday is on the second of May.
On Mondays I work at home.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: Θα έρθω ___ Δευτέρα.
I will come on Monday.
exercises.explanation: Θα έρθω τη Δευτέρα. — I will come on Monday. A definite accusative weekday can place an event on a day, as in τη Δευτέρα, while στις plus a numeral expresses many calendar dates. Month names commonly appear in the genitive after a date; recurring weekdays can also use plural forms such as τις Δευτέρες.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: Τα γενέθλιά μου είναι ___ δύο Μαΐου.
My birthday is on the second of May.
exercises.explanation: Τα γενέθλιά μου είναι στις δύο Μαΐου. — My birthday is on the second of May. A definite accusative weekday can place an event on a day, as in τη Δευτέρα, while στις plus a numeral expresses many calendar dates. Month names commonly appear in the genitive after a date; recurring weekdays can also use plural forms such as τις Δευτέρες.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: ___ Δευτέρες δουλεύω στο σπίτι.
On Mondays I work at home.
exercises.explanation: Τις Δευτέρες δουλεύω στο σπίτι. — On Mondays I work at home. A definite accusative weekday can place an event on a day, as in τη Δευτέρα, while στις plus a numeral expresses many calendar dates. Month names commonly appear in the genitive after a date; recurring weekdays can also use plural forms such as τις Δευτέρες.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase explicitly means recurring “on Fridays”?
exercises.explanation: Plural τις Παρασκευές expresses Fridays as a recurring time.

exercises.prompt: Complete the date: στις τρεις ___. (“on the third of June”)
exercises.explanation: The month follows the date in genitive singular: Ιουνίου.

title: Addressing someone: the vocative
explanation: The vocative is used when directly addressing a person and normally has no article. Common masculine names lose final -ς, as in Νίκος → Νίκο, and some -ος nouns use -ε, as in φίλος → φίλε; feminine and neuter forms often remain unchanged.
formation: Νίκος → Νίκο; φίλος → φίλε; Μαρία → Μαρία

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: ___, έλα εδώ.
Nikos, come here.
exercises.explanation: Νίκο, έλα εδώ. — Nikos, come here. The vocative is used when directly addressing a person and normally has no article. Common masculine names lose final -ς, as in Νίκος → Νίκο, and some -ος nouns use -ε, as in φίλος → φίλε; feminine and neuter forms often remain unchanged.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: ___ μου, σε ευχαριστώ.

exercises.explanation: Φίλε μου, σε ευχαριστώ. — My friend, thank you. The vocative is used when directly addressing a person and normally has no article. Common masculine names lose final -ς, as in Νίκος → Νίκο, and some -ος nouns use -ε, as in φίλος → φίλε; feminine and neuter forms often remain unchanged.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: ___, πού είσαι;
Petros, where are you?
exercises.explanation: Πέτρο, πού είσαι; — Petros, where are you? The vocative is used when directly addressing a person and normally has no article. Common masculine names lose final -ς, as in Νίκος → Νίκο, and some -ος nouns use -ε, as in φίλος → φίλε; feminine and neuter forms often remain unchanged.

exercises.prompt: Choose a direct address to Nikos.
exercises.explanation: Direct address uses the vocative Νίκο without the definite article.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses Μαρία as direct address?
choices: Το βιβλίο της Μαρίας είναι εδώ.
exercises.explanation: The comma and command show direct address; feminine Μαρία keeps its form.

title: Nobody, nothing and nowhere
explanation: Κανείς/κανένας, τίποτα and πουθενά combine with δεν in negative indicative statements, giving Greek negative concord. In questions these words can have “any” meanings, so do not assign them an automatically negative translation in every context.
formation: δεν + verb + κανέναν / τίποτα / πουθενά; κανείς + δεν + verb

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: ___ ξέρω τίποτα.
I do not know anything.
exercises.explanation: Δεν ξέρω τίποτα. — I do not know anything. Κανείς/κανένας, τίποτα and πουθενά combine with δεν in negative indicative statements, giving Greek negative concord. In questions these words can have “any” meanings, so do not assign them an automatically negative translation in every context.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: Κανείς ___ ήρθε.
Nobody came.
exercises.explanation: Κανείς δεν ήρθε. — Nobody came. Κανείς/κανένας, τίποτα and πουθενά combine with δεν in negative indicative statements, giving Greek negative concord. In questions these words can have “any” meanings, so do not assign them an automatically negative translation in every context.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: Δεν είδα ___.
I did not see anyone.
exercises.explanation: Δεν είδα κανέναν. — I did not see anyone. Κανείς/κανένας, τίποτα and πουθενά combine with δεν in negative indicative statements, giving Greek negative concord. In questions these words can have “any” meanings, so do not assign them an automatically negative translation in every context.

exercises.prompt: Choose the standard negative statement “I am not going anywhere”.
exercises.explanation: Πουθενά occurs with δεν in the ordinary negative indicative statement.

exercises.prompt: In Θέλεις τίποτα;, which interpretation is natural?
exercises.explanation: In this question τίποτα has an “anything” interpretation rather than asserting nothing.

title: Someone, something and somewhere
explanation: Κάποιος/κάποια/κάποιο refer to an unspecified person or thing and change for gender, number and case. Κάτι means “something” and κάπου means “somewhere”; neither inflects like κάποιος, so choose the form for the intended role.
formation: κάποιος / κάποια / κάποιο; object κάποιον; invariable κάτι / κάπου

examples.translation: Someone is knocking at the door.
I saw someone in the garden.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: ___ χτυπάει την πόρτα.
Someone is knocking at the door.
exercises.explanation: Κάποιος χτυπάει την πόρτα. — Someone is knocking at the door. Κάποιος/κάποια/κάποιο refer to an unspecified person or thing and change for gender, number and case. Κάτι means “something” and κάπου means “somewhere”; neither inflects like κάποιος, so choose the form for the intended role.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: Θέλω ___ να φάω.
I want something to eat.
exercises.explanation: Θέλω κάτι να φάω. — I want something to eat. Κάποιος/κάποια/κάποιο refer to an unspecified person or thing and change for gender, number and case. Κάτι means “something” and κάπου means “somewhere”; neither inflects like κάποιος, so choose the form for the intended role.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the sentence to match the English meaning: Είδα ___ στον κήπο.
I saw someone in the garden.
exercises.explanation: Είδα κάποιον στον κήπο. — I saw someone in the garden. Κάποιος/κάποια/κάποιο refer to an unspecified person or thing and change for gender, number and case. Κάτι means “something” and κάπου means “somewhere”; neither inflects like κάποιος, so choose the form for the intended role.

exercises.prompt: Choose “The keys are somewhere here”.
exercises.explanation: Κάπου is the invariable adverb referring to an unspecified place.

exercises.prompt: Complete the subject: ___ γυναίκα σε περιμένει.
exercises.explanation: The indefinite word agrees with feminine singular γυναίκα: κάποια.
